deep.reconstruction:
Setting and notation. Euler studies double sums of the form Σ_x x^{-m}(1+2^{-n}+…+x^{-n}). In modern notation these are non-strict double zeta values ζ*(m,n) = ζ(m,n) + ζ(m+n), where ζ(a,b) = Σ_{x>y} x^{-a} y^{-b}. On these pages, for a fixed weight N = m+n:
- q^k means ζ*(k, N−k), i.e. Σ x^{-k} H_x^{(N−k)}.
- p^k means the product ζ(k)ζ(N−k) for 1<k<N.
- p^N means ζ(N).
- q^1 and p^1 are formally divergent.
The superscripts are labels, not powers. Euler's 'third method' gives linear relations among the q's. The basic one is q^k + q^{N−k} = p^k + p^N, the stuffle relation ζ*(a,b) + ζ*(b,a) = ζ(a)ζ(b) + ζ(a+b). He then solves the resulting linear system order by order.

Order N=8 (top of the page). Line 1, q^7 = 9/2 p^8 − p^2 − p^3 − 1/2 p^4, is Euler's evaluation Σ H_n/n^7 = (1+7/2)ζ(8) − ½ Σ_{k=2}^{6} ζ(k)ζ(8−k). It is correct. Line 3, q^7 = p^2 − p^3 + 1/2 p^4, is equivalent to line 1 because 9/2 ζ(8) = 2ζ(2)ζ(6) + ζ(4)^2. That identity holds: 10/3 + 7/6 = 9/2.

Euler then states that all remaining equations collapse into one relation, 4q^5 + 10q^6 = 20p^3 − 9p^4, after using 7ζ(8) = 6ζ(4)^2. The p^3 reading is my correction; see the transcription notes. I verified this by double shuffle. Modulo products, stuffle and shuffle in weight 8 leave exactly one relation, 2ζ(5,3) + 5ζ(6,2) ≡ 0. Exactly, the shuffle for ζ(2)ζ(6) gives 5ζ(6,2) + 2ζ(5,3) = 12ζ(2)ζ(6) + 10ζ(3)ζ(5) + 9/2 ζ(4)^2 − 75/2 ζ(8). Hence:
- 4q^5 + 10q^6 = 24ζ(2)ζ(6) + 20ζ(3)ζ(5) + 9ζ(4)^2 − 61ζ(8).
- With ζ(2)ζ(6) = 5/3 ζ(8) and ζ(4)^2 = 7/6 ζ(8), this equals 20ζ(3)ζ(5) − 21/2 ζ(8) = 20p^3 − 9p^4.

So Euler isolates precisely the reducible combination. He correctly concludes that the method does not determine q^5 and q^6 individually. Today we know that ζ(5,3) is the first (conjecturally irreducible) new double zeta value, so that conclusion is right.

Order N=9. Here the system has a unique solution, giving all of q^8, …, q^2 as rational combinations of ζ(9), ζ(2)ζ(7), ζ(3)ζ(6) and ζ(4)ζ(5). This is the odd-weight reduction theorem for double zeta values. I checked q^8 against Euler's linear formula. All pairings q^k + q^{9−k} = p^k + p^9 hold coefficient by coefficient.

Order 10 is skipped. Order N=11 is solved fully, continuing on the next page. Every pair q^k + q^{11−k} = p^k + p^11 again checks coefficient by coefficient. The next page then extracts a recursion, j·c_j = (N+1−j)·c_{j−1} ± (N+1)/2, for the ζ(N) coefficients.
errors: Order 8, second expression for q^7: as printed/transcribed, −9/2 p^8 + 3p^2 − p^3 + 1/2 p^4 is not equal to the true value. That value is p^2 − p^3 + 1/2 p^4 (equivalently 9/2 p^8 − p^2 − p^3 − 1/2 p^4). The p^4 coefficient must be +3/2 for consistency, via 2ζ(2)ζ(6) + ζ(4)^2 = 9/2 ζ(8). Either the scan's small fraction is 3/2, or there is a misprint. Note that the printed third line equals the average of the first two only if the second has +1/2, so the printed lines are mutually inconsistent.

The odd-weight tables (N=9, N=11) pass all internal stuffle-pair checks, and q^8 for N=9 agrees with Euler's linear formula. I did not independently verify every N=9 and N=11 coefficient against the closed-form Borwein–Borwein–Girgensohn formula.

ideas.what: Evaluation of Σ H_n/n^{N−1} (q^{N−1}) in terms of ζ(N) and products
ideas.modern_name: Euler's linear sum formula ζ(N−1,1) = (N/2)ζ(N) − ½Σζ(k)ζ(N−k) (up to ζ*(·) convention)

ideas.what: Weight 8: the stuffle/shuffle system leaves one undetermined quantity; only 4q^5 + 10q^6, i.e. 2ζ(5,3) + 5ζ(6,2) + 7ζ(8), is reducible to products
ideas.modern_name: Double-shuffle relations in weight 8; ζ(5,3) as the first irreducible double zeta value
ideas.usually_credited_to: Irreducibility conjectured and studied by Borwein–Bradley–Broadhurst, Zagier et al. (1990s); Euler's failure at even weight is noted in histories

ideas.what: Use of ζ(4)^2 = 7/6 ζ(8), i.e. 7p^8 = 6p^4, to simplify
ideas.modern_name: Rationality of ζ(2k)/π^{2k} (Euler's even zeta values)

ideas.what: Complete reduction of all double sums of odd weight 9 and 11 to ζ(N) and products of single zetas

missed.claim: In weight 8, Euler explicitly identifies the unique reducible linear combination of the undetermined double sums: 4ζ*(5,3) + 10ζ*(6,2) = 20ζ(3)ζ(5) − 9ζ(4)^2. In modern form, 2ζ(5,3) + 5ζ(6,2) is reducible, while the individual values are not determined by his relations. This is the modern statement that the weight-8 double-shuffle relations leave exactly one free parameter. Histories usually say only that Euler 'failed' for even weights; this exact identity and its correctness are seldom credited to him.
missed.quote: reliquae aequationes omnes coalescunt in hanc vnicam: 4q^5 + 10q^6 = 20p^3 − 9p^4 ob 7p^8 = 6p^4
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is a historical precedent for computing the dimension of the space of double zeta values modulo products in weight 8 (one new generator). Euler effectively did this computation in 1776; it is relevant to accounts of the prehistory of double-shuffle theory.

deep.surprise_reason: The odd-weight reductions and Euler's even-weight failure in E477 are well known. The explicit, correct weight-8 reducible combination 2ζ(5,3) + 5ζ(6,2) is a nice detail. It is probably rarely highlighted but likely known to MZV historians such as Borwein and Bradley.
transcription_corrections: Order 8 relation: '20p^8' should read '20p^3'. The superscript 3 resembles 8 in this print; mathematically the right side is 20ζ(3)ζ(5) − 9ζ(4)^2. Similarly, the mark '4ʳᵉ' after 9p is just p^4.
Second q^7 line for order 8: the p^4 coefficient should be +3/2 (printed or read as 1/2).
The running head reads 'MEDITATIONES CIRCA' (the transcription has 'MEDIATIONES').
Order 9, first line: 'q^8 = +5p^9 − p^2 − p^3 − p^4' is correct (the image shows q^8).
